The '''2016–17 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kentucky]] in the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games in [[Lexington, Kentucky]] for the 41st consecutive season at [[Rupp Arena]], with a capacity of 20,500.  The team, led by [[John Calipari]] in his eighth season as head coach, was a member of the [[Southeastern Conference]].

[[Bam Adebayo|Edrice Adebayo]], nicknamed "Bam" and originally from [[Pinetown, North Carolina]], was a consensus top 15 player in his class. He committed to Kentucky on November 17, live on ESPN's ''[[Mike & Mike]]'' simulcast radio show.<ref name=BAMcommit>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/14152175/edrice-bam-adebayo-commits-kentucky-wildcats|title=No. 6 recruit Edrice 'Bam' Adebayo commits to Kentucky|access-date=2015-11-17|date=2015-11-17|publisher=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> He chose Kentucky over [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] and [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]]. He is ranked in the top 10 by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] (No. 6) and [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]] (No. 6). 247Sports (No. 14) and [[Scout.com|Scout]] (No. 15) tab him as a top-15 prospect in the 2016 class. He has prior USA Basketball experience and was named a [[MaxPreps.com|MaxPreps]] All-American in 2013.<ref name=Fallsignees>{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/news/kentucky-men-s-basketball-signs-six-in-fall-signing-11-19-2015|title=Kentucky Men's Basketball Signs Six in Fall Signing Period|access-date=2015-11-19|date=2014-11-19|publisher=University of Kentucky|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170328005752/http://www.ukathletics.com/news/kentucky-men-s-basketball-signs-six-in-fall-signing-11-19-2015|archive-date=2017-03-28}}</ref>

[[De'Aaron Fox]], originally from [[Katy, Texas]], was the second highest rated point guard that Calipari had signed at Kentucky. He committed to Kentucky on November 12, live on [[ESPNU]].<ref name=DFcommit>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/14115542/deaaron-fox-no-7-espn-100-commits-kentucky-wildcats|title=Point guard De'Aaron Fox, No. 7 in ESPN 100, chooses Kentucky|access-date=2015-11-12|date=2015-11-12|publisher=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> He chose Kentucky over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], and [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]]. He was the nation's consensus top point guard, was ranked the consensus No. 3 overall player by the four main recruiting services [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]], [[Scout.com|Scout]], and 247 Sports.<ref name="Fallsignees" />

[[Wenyen Gabriel]], originally from [[Manchester, New Hampshire]], was the third commitment in the Kentucky class. He committed to Kentucky on October 1, live on the radio.<ref name=WGcommit>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/13784752/kentucky-wildcats-land-recruit-wenyen-gabriel|title=No. 23-rated Wenyen Gabriel chooses Kentucky over Duke, others|access-date=2015-10-01|date=2015-10-01|publisher=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> He chose Kentucky over [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], and [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]]. He was a consensus five star prospect, and was ranked the consensus No. 17 overall player by the four main recruiting services [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]], [[Scout.com|Scout]], and 247 Sports.<ref name="Fallsignees" />

[[Sacha Killeya-Jones]], originally from [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina]], was the second commitment in the Kentucky class. He committed to Kentucky on October 1, live on the radio.<ref name=SKJcommit>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/13467026/recruit-sacha-killeya-jones-commits-kentucky-wildcats|title=Sacha Killeya-Jones commits to Kentucky Wildcats|access-date=2015-08-26|date=2015-08-26|publisher=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> He chose Kentucky over [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]]. He was a consensus four star prospect, and was ranked the consensus No. 36 overall player by the four main recruiting services [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]], [[Scout.com|Scout]], and 247 Sports.<ref name="Fallsignees" />

[[Malik Monk]], originally from [[Lepanto, Arkansas]] but attending high school in [[Bentonville, Arkansas]], was the second highest rated shooting guard that Calipari signed at Kentucky. He committed to Kentucky on November 18.<ref name=MMcommit>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/14161493/no-5-recruit-malik-monk-commits-kentucky-wildcats|title=No. 5 recruit Malik Monk commits to Kentucky|access-date=2015-11-18|date=2015-11-18|publisher=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> He chose Kentucky over [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] where his brother, [[Marcus Monk]], played college basketball and football. He was a consensus five star prospect, and was ranked the consensus No. 5 overall player by the four main recruiting services [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]], [[Scout.com|Scout]], and 247 Sports.<ref name="Fallsignees" />

===Accolades and rankings===
The [[Southeastern Conference]] preseason media poll was released at the SEC Media Days in October, it predicted that Kentucky would win the championship.<ref name="Preseason media">{{cite press release|url=http://www.secsports.com/article/17829950/media-picks-uk-win-2017-sec-championship |title=Media picks Kentucky to win 2017 SEC Championship |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=October 19, 2016 |access-date=October 19, 2016}}</ref> Adebayo and Fox were named to the All-SEC First Team while Briscoe and Monk were named to the All-SEC Second Team.<ref name="Preseason media" />

''USA Today'' announced its initial coaches poll on October 15 with Kentucky ranked as No. 4 in the country.<ref name="coaches_pre">{{cite news |url=http://sportspolls.usatoday.com/ncaa/basketball-men/polls/coaches-poll/2016/1/|title=Top 25 Teams, Week 1 |work=USA Today |date=October 20, 2016}}</ref> The [[Associated Press]] announced on October 31 that Kentucky was ranked No. 2 to start the season in its initial poll of the season.<ref name="AP_pre">{{cite web |url=http://collegebasketball.ap.org/poll/2017/1 |title=The AP Top 25 Poll |work=[[Associated Press|AP]] |date=October 31, 2016}}</ref>

===Events===
On July 18 Kentucky released the non-conference portion of its schedule.<ref name=schedule>{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/news/uk-mbb-faces-challenging-nonconference-schedule-in-2016-17-07-18-2016l|title=UK MBB Faces Challenging Nonconference Schedule in 2016-17|access-date=2016-07-18|date=2016-07-18|publisher=JMI Sports|work=UKathletics.com}}{{Dead link|date=April 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The schedule is highlighted by marquee match-ups at Rupp Arena and across the country. Kentucky will travel to New York to play Michigan State in the annual Champions Classic, to the Bahamas to play Arizona State, back to New York to play Hofstra, to Las Vegas to play against North Carolina in the annual CBS Sports Classic, and finally to Louisville to face in-state rival Louisville.. Kentucky will also host UCLA for the first time as well as Kansas in the Big 12/SEC Challenge.

Tickets for Big Blue Madness, Kentucky's version of Midnight Madness went on sale and sold out on September 30.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/news/big-blue-madness-tickets-sold-out-09-30-2016|title=Madness Tickets SOLD OUT|access-date=2016-09-30|date=2016-09-30|publisher=JMI Sports|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161019212343/http://www.ukathletics.com/news/big-blue-madness-tickets-sold-out-09-30-2016|archive-date=2016-10-19|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Big Blue Madness took place on October 14. The event debuted the team for the 2016–17 season. It included player introductions, a speech by Calipari, and a scrimmage.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/kentuckys-big-blue-madness-highlighted-by-cousins-vs-wall-at-rupp-arena/|title=Kentucky's Big Blue Madness highlighted by Cousins vs. Wall at Rupp Arena|access-date=2016-10-14|date=2016-10-14|publisher=CBS Sports|author=Norlander, Matt}}</ref>

==2017–18 newcomers==
[[Nick Richards]], a native of [[Kingston, Jamaica]] living in [[Queens|Queens, New York]], was the first commitment in the Kentucky class. He committed to Kentucky on November 10 at a press conference at his high school.<ref name=NRPWcommit-2>{{cite news|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article114023728.html|title=Kentucky lands commitments from a pair of five-star basketball recruits|access-date=2016-11-10|date=2016-11-10|newspaper=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]}}</ref> He chose Kentucky over [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]]. He was a consensus five star prospect, and was ranked the consensus No. 14 overall player by the four main recruiting services.

[[P. J. Washington]], a [[Dallas]] native attending school in [[Las Vegas Valley|Las Vegas, Nevada]], was the second commitment in the Kentucky class. He committed to Kentucky on November 10 live on [[ESPNU]].<ref name="NRPWcommit-2" /> He chose Kentucky over [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] and [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]]. He was a consensus five star prospect, and was ranked the consensus No. 15 overall player by the four main recruiting services.

[[Shai Gilgeous-Alexander]], originally from [[Hamilton, Ontario]] and attending school in [[Chattanooga, Tennessee]], was the third commitment in the Kentucky class.  He committed to Kentucky on November 14 through a message on [[Twitter]].<ref name=NRPWcommit>{{cite news|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article114610083.html|title=Calipari adds third commitment to Kentucky's recruiting class of 2017|access-date=2016-11-14|date=2016-11-14|newspaper=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]}}</ref>  He was a consensus top fifty player, ranked No. 42 by the four main recruiting services [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]], [[Scout.com|Scout]], and 24/7 Sports.

[[Quade Green]], from [[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]], was the fourth commitment in the Kentucky class. He signed his National Letter of Intent on November 16, the last day of the early signing period, but did not reveal his choice between Kentucky and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] until an event at his high school on November 19 - with his mother Tamika Johnson by his side.<ref name=greencommit>{{Cite news |last=Roberts |first=Ben |title=New UK commitment Quade Green will bring 'Philly toughness' to Lexington |newspaper=Lexington Herald-Leader |date=November 19, 2016 |url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article115990473.html |access-date=November 21, 2016}}</ref> He was a consensus top-25 player and ranked as a five-star player by the four main recruiting services [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]], [[Scout.com|Scout]], and 24/7 Sports.

[[Hamidou Diallo]], a Queens native who graduated from a Connecticut school in spring 2016, announced on January 7, 2017, that he would enroll at UK for the start of the school's spring semester the following week. While he was eligible to play immediately, he redshirted the spring semester and is set to begin play as a freshman in 2017–18.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/18427587/five-star-wing-hamidou-diallo-commits-kentucky-wildcats-enroll-next-week |title=Hamidou Diallo, No. 11 in ESPN 100, picks Kentucky over UConn |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |publisher=ESPN.com |date=January 7, 2017 |access-date=January 7, 2017}}</ref>

Jemarl Baker, a native of [[Eastvale, California]], was the seventh commitment in the Kentucky recruiting class. He announced his decision on April 11 via a story posted on Scout.com by Evan Daniels.<ref name=bakecommit>{{Cite news |last=Daniels |first=Evan |title=Four-star guard Jemarl Baker commits to Kentucky |website=Scout |date=April 11, 2017|url=http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/story/1769972-jemarl-baker-commits-kentucky |access-date=April 11, 2017}}</ref> Baker originally committed to [[Cuonzo Martin]] at [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], before Martin left the school to coach [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]]. He averaged 17.1 points, 4.1 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 1.8 steals for Roosevelt High School in Corona, Calif., and he quickly emerged as one of the Wildcats' top backcourt targets after their season ended last month. Scout.com ranks Baker as the No. 86 overall prospect in the 2017 class.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Roberts|first1=Ben|title=New basketball commitment Jemarl Baker is 'exactly what Kentucky needed'|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article143944139.html|newspaper=Lexington Herald-Leader|access-date=April 24, 2017}}</ref>

UK's final commitment came on May 6, when [[Tampa, Florida|Tampa]] product [[Kevin Knox II]] announced he would come to the school. Kentucky beat out Duke, Florida State, North Carolina, and Missouri for Knox's signature.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/19326360/kevin-knox-five-star-recruit-chooses-kentucky-florida-state-duke-north-carolina |title=Kevin Knox, No. 9-ranked prospect in 2017, commits to Kentucky |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |publisher=ESPN.com |date=May 6, 2017 |access-date=May 6, 2017}}</ref>

==Honors==

===Weekly Awards===
On November 14 Fox was named SEC Freshman of the Week following a 21-point career-high against Canisius and a 12-assist career-high against Stephen F. Austin.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/news/de-aaron-fox-named-sec-freshman-of-the-week-11-14-2016|title=De'Aaron Fox Named SEC Freshman of the Week|access-date=2015-11-14|date=2015-11-14|publisher=JMI Sports|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161115132213/http://www.ukathletics.com/news/de-aaron-fox-named-sec-freshman-of-the-week-11-14-2016|archive-date=2016-11-15|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===National Awards===
On March 28, 2017, Malik Monk was voted consensus Second Team All-American by each of the NCAA's four recognized organizations (AP, National Association of Basketball Coaches, United States Basketball Writers Association, Sporting News) it uses to determine consensus status.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/news/monk-earns-consensus-all-america-second-team-status-with-ap-honor-03-28-2017|title=Monk Earns Consensus All-America Second Team Status with AP Honor|access-date=2017-04-14|date=2017-03-28|publisher=UK Athletics|work=UKAthletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170408072815/http://www.ukathletics.com/news/monk-earns-consensus-all-america-second-team-status-with-ap-honor-03-28-2017|archive-date=2017-04-08|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 7, 2017, Malik Monk won the [[Jerry West Award]], which is awarded to the nation's top shooting guard of the year. Monk beat out Duke's [[Luke Kennard (basketball)|Luke Kennard]], UCLA's [[Bryce Alford]], and Creighton's Marcus Foster for the award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article143460969.html|title=Malik Monk wins Jerry West Award as nation's best shooting guard|access-date=2017-04-14|date=2017-04-07|publisher=Lexington Herald-Leader|work=kentucky.com}}</ref>
